proposals.before: the Dowager Empress was held prisoner in Chu yet asked for soup as calmly as ever.
proposals.after: the Grand Emperor was held prisoner in Chu yet asked for soup as calmly as ever.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太上 here is the Grand Emperor (Han Gaozu's father), not a Dowager Empress.

proposals.before: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xuan of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
proposals.after: Gao Cheng then had Cui Xian of the Ministry of Personnel appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief; he impeached the powerful without sparing any, custom was renewed, and private wrongdoing and bribery ceased.
proposals.reason: 崔暹 is standardly Cui Xian (暹 xiān), not Cui Xuan.

proposals.before: At the time Prince of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
proposals.after: At the time Duke of Taiyuan Gao Yang was at the Twin Hall east of the city; he entered and punished the traitors, dismembering Jing and the rest and lacquering their heads.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太原公 is Duke of Taiyuan, matching s0029; Prince overstates the title.

proposals.before: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, the ten rebels of Zhou fell; Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs—the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.
proposals.after: Yet when the hundred millions of the Yi people submitted, Zhou's ten capable ministers prevailed; King Zhou's hundred victories in the end left him without heirs—the battle at Yingchuan is the warning of Yin.
proposals.reason: 十亂 are Zhou's capable ministers, distinct from 紂 (King Zhou); the English conflates both as Zhou.

decisions.reason: s0104’s 太上, paired with Wang Ling’s mother in Chu, is the Grand Emperor (太上皇, Han Gaozu’s father), not a Dowager Empress; the proposed replacement restores the correct identity without other change.
s0017 names 崔暹; 暹 is xiān, so Cui Xian is the standard reading and Cui Xuan is a real romanization error, not a stylistic preference.
s0157 has 太原公洋; 公 is Duke, not Prince (王), so Duke of Taiyuan corrects an overstated title while leaving the rest of the sentence intact.

s0083 contrasts 十亂 (Zhou’s ten capable ministers, 亂臣) with 紂之百克 (King Zhou of Shang’s hundred victories); the original wrongly turns 十亂 into “ten rebels” and collapses both figures into “Zhou.” The proposal separates them accurately.

claimRevisions.reason: Accepted r0001 shows English Dowager Empress came only from the mistranslation of 太上; the title claim must read Grand Emperor while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
Accepted r0002 shows English Cui Xuan came only from the bad romanization of 崔暹; the personal-name claim must read Cui Xian while keeping zh, pinyin, id, subject, predicate, certainty, and evidence.
